CANONICAL_NAME.value: Linux TCP congestion control -- CUBIC and BBR (the congestion-avoidance lineage under pressure)

value.lineage: TCP congestion control (1988-, Van Jacobson onward): Tahoe -> Reno -> NewReno -> CUBIC (2008, loss-based, the Linux default) -> BBR (2016, Google, model-based rate/RTT). Each redesign was forced by a changed network: higher bandwidth-delay products, then bufferbloat. Preserved here as the actual Linux kernel modules tcp_cubic.c and tcp_bbr.c.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: congestion avoidance on a shared network

value.built_to: regulate a TCP sender's transmission rate so it uses available bandwidth without collapsing the shared network -- inferring congestion from loss (CUBIC) or from a bandwidth/RTT model (BBR)
value.pressure: a shared link of unknown, varying capacity with many competing senders; too fast causes loss and congestion collapse, too slow wastes the link
value.success_means: high throughput, low queueing delay, and fairness to other flows across a range of bandwidth-delay products and loss rates

value.pressure: bandwidth scarcity, packet loss, variable RTT, bufferbloat, competing flows
value.failure_condition: congestion collapse (1986): everyone retransmits into a saturated link and useful throughput drops toward zero
